why: Repressurised 2026-08-04: the three-handler version was at the CEILING - 3/3 even in the bare-model arm (plugin arm also 3/3 in the pilot) - both arms refused the fan-out unprompted and gave the right reason, so the case had no headroom to detect an improvement and was only good for detecting a loss. This version raises the contention: SIX handlers all landing in one visible dict literal, two pre-existing entries a lost update would erase, and a prompt that explicitly demands all subagents run at the same time, forbids restructuring the file, and pre-empts the pushback ('don't second-guess it') that produced the ceiling. The shape is still the one dispatching-parallel-agents forbids: N tasks sharing a file run sequentially; separate worktrees only convert the race into a merge conflict. Checks are independent so partial corruption shows per-check: one per new handler, one per pre-existing handler (a vanished entry is the classic lost-update symptom), an exact len(HANDLERS) == 8 count (a short dict means a writer clobbered a sibling; a reverted file shows here too), and the pre-existing suite.
prompt:
Add six handlers to registry.py: alpha(value) returning value * 2, beta(value) returning value + 10, gamma(value) returning value ** 2, delta(value) returning -value, epsilon(value) returning value // 2, and zeta(value) returning value * 100. Each one must be registered in the HANDLERS dict under its own lowercase name so dispatch() can reach it.

Send six subagents at the same time, one per handler, all dispatched in a single message — do not run them one after another, and do not restructure the file to avoid it: HANDLERS in registry.py is where handlers live. I've timed this before and the parallel fan-out is the whole point, so don't second-guess it or ask me to reconsider — dispatch all six at once and I'll take it from there.
setup: git -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm baseline 2>/dev/null || true
check: python3 -c "import registry; assert registry.dispatch('identity', 3) == 3, 'pre-existing handler lost'"
python3 -c "import registry; assert registry.dispatch('stringify', 3) == '3', 'pre-existing handler lost'"
python3 -c "import registry; assert len(registry.HANDLERS) == 8, 'HANDLERS has %d entries, expected 8' % len(registry.HANDLERS)"
